title: John Abraham Starts Shooting Ribhu Dasgupta’s Psychological Thriller ‘Guru’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Principal photography has commenced on “Guru,” a Bollywood psychological thriller starring John Abraham and directed by Ribhu Dasgupta. 

	The film
body:
Principal photography has commenced on “Guru,” a Bollywood psychological thriller starring John Abraham and directed by Ribhu Dasgupta. 

	The film also stars Danish Pandor, Arif Zakaria and Kitu Gidwani.

	Dasgupta is known for his work in the thriller genre. His credits include the Netflix series “Bard of Blood,” as well as “Girl on the Train” and “Te3n.” He is also attached to the upcoming “Section 84 IPC.”


	Set against a backdrop of unsettling mystery, “Guru” follows a man whose life begins to change when he realizes that something is not right, and that his memory and his reality are two distinct things. As strange events unfold around him, he starts questioning his own perception of reality and wondering whom he can rely on. The story brings together Abraham, Pandor, Zakaria and Gidwani in a plot where memory and reality steadily converge.
	

	“The world of ‘Guru’ is unsettling. Anything which has depth in terms of story, treatment and performance, at the same time gives you something to relish, excites and challenges a filmmaker. I have been wanting to collaborate with John for a long time and ‘Guru’ is that script with that destiny,” Dasgupta said.

	“‘Guru’ is the kind of story that stays with you long after you’ve read it. What drew me to the film was the uncertainty at its core – when you can’t trust your own memory, reality itself becomes a question. The storyline is layered, unsettling and deeply intriguing, and I’m excited for audiences to experience it,” Abraham added.

	The film is produced by Authum Entertainment, Shibasish Sarkar, JA Entertainment and Fusion Flicks.

schema.headline: John Abraham Starts Shooting Ribhu Dasgupta’s Psychological Thriller ‘Guru’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Helicopter Crashes Near Site of Deadly Metro Bus Accident in Chatsworth
description: NBCLA’s NewsChopper4 helicopter crashed Tuesday night in Chatsworth, just blocks away from an L.A. Metro bus crash that killed two people and sent s
body:
NBCLA’s NewsChopper4 helicopter crashed Tuesday night in Chatsworth, just blocks away from an L.A. Metro bus crash that killed two people and sent six others to the hospital.

	NBC4 Los Angeles reported Tuesday night on the incident and indicated that the crash was in connection with the station. KNBC-TV news anchor Colleen Williams said on air shortly after the incident, “We know that it is a news helicopter, and we know that we have lost contact” with the station’s helicopter.
	

	Authorities with the Los Angeles Fire Department told KTLA that the helicopter went down between two commercial buildings at 9151 N. Mason Avenue just before 7 p.m. PT. 

	CBS News reports that the helicopter appeared to crash onto two shipping containers, as well as several vehicles that were parked in the vicinity. While it’s unclear how many people were on the helicopter when it went down, the outlet reported that three people were killed in the crash

	“We do have one confirmed patient that seemed to be outside of the helicopter when it crashed,” said LAFD Captain Branden Silverman to CBS. “That person was declared deceased on scene. … At this point, we have not confirmed how many victims, or how many people, were inside the helicopter.”

	According to the Los Angeles Times, the Metro accident occurred around 5 p.m. PT when an SUV crashed into the bus, which was traveling on Line 166, trapping the passengers inside. Jennifer Middleton, a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Fire Department, told the outlet that the two individuals who were killed were pronounced dead at the scene.

schema.headline: Helicopter Crashes Near Site of Deadly Metro Bus Accident in Chatsworth

title: Oscars: Indonesia Selects Kamila Andini’s ‘Four Seasons in Java’ for International Feature Race (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Indonesia has selected Kamila Andini‘s “Four Seasons in Java” (“Empat Musim Pertiwi”) as its submission for the international feature category at th
body:
Indonesia has selected Kamila Andini‘s “Four Seasons in Java” (“Empat Musim Pertiwi”) as its submission for the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards.

	Written and directed by Andini and produced by Ifa Isfansyah for Forka Films, the film stars Putri Marino, Arya Saloka, Christine Hakim and Hana Malasan. The story centers on Pertiwi (Marino), a formerly incarcerated woman who comes back to a hometown that will not welcome her, pushing her to reckon with a painful personal history set against ongoing silence, violence and social division. Elements of mystery, magical realism and science fiction run through the psychological drama as it examines trauma, memory and what it takes to reclaim a sense of home and identity.
	

	Andini said, “‘Four Seasons in Java’ is a story about returning, not only to a place, but to the parts of ourselves that we have been forced to leave behind. It is deeply rooted in Indonesia, but the questions it asks about trauma, memory, violence and healing are universal. I am incredibly honored that the film will represent Indonesia at the Academy Awards.”


	The selection extends Andini’s run as one of Indonesian cinema’s most consistent presences on the international festival circuit. Her 2021 feature “Yuni” premiered at the Toronto Film Festival, where it won the Platform Prize, and went on to become Indonesia’s Oscars submission that year. Her film “Before, Now & Then” (Nana) played in competition at the Berlin International Film Festival, where Laura Basuki won the Silver Bear for best supporting performance.

	“Four Seasons in Java” had its world premiere in the Centrepiece program at the ongoing Toronto Film Festival and is set to screen at the Busan International Film Festival next month. It has also picked up a best cinematography nomination at the 2026 Asian Pacific Screen Awards.
	

	Isfansyah said, “We are incredibly proud that ‘Four Seasons in Java’ will represent Indonesia at the Academy Awards. Kamila has created a film that is profoundly Indonesian in its setting and perspective, while speaking to universal experiences of trauma, resilience and the search for belonging. We are grateful to our international partners and to everyone who has supported the film’s journey.”

	The film is an international co-production spanning Indonesia, France, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Saudi Arabia and Singapore. Paris-based Goodfellas is handling worldwide sales. “Four Seasons in Java” is set for a wide theatrical release in Indonesia on Oct. 8, following an earlier run in select theaters this September.

title: Busan Names Jury Members for Mecenat, Sonje, Netpac, Fipresci Awards
description: The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has finalized jury members across four award categories: the BIFF Mecenat Award, the Sonje Award,
body:
The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has finalized jury members across four award categories: the BIFF Mecenat Award, the Sonje Award, the Netpac Award and the Fipresci Award.

	The BIFF Mecenat Award, which goes to a standout Korean or Asian documentary in Wide Angle Competition and carries a prize of KRW10 million ($7,300), will be judged by Rintu Thomas, Kim Taeil and Zhou Hao. Thomas co-directed “Writing With Fire” (2021), which picked up a Peabody Award, an Oscar nomination and two Sundance prizes. Kim, who has spent years on his ongoing People’s World History project, running from “No Name Stars” (2010) through “Again the Wind Blows” (2022), previously won the Woonpa Award and the BIFF Mecenat Award itself for “Annyong, Sayonara” (2005) and “Raining Dust” (2025). Zhou, a former journalist, has built a body of observational work tracking ordinary lives and urban change, including “Cotton” (2014) and “The Chinese Mayor” (2015), the latter a prizewinner at the Golden Horse Film Festival, Sundance and the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam.
	

	The Sonje Award, honoring an outstanding Korean or Asian short film in Wide Angle Competition with the same KRW10 million ($7,300) prize, will be decided by Anuparna Roy, Abinash Bikram Shah and Lee Ranhee. Roy’s “Songs of Forgotten Trees” (2025) and “Lovers in the Blue Night” (2026) both debuted in the Horizons section at Venice and won awards. Shah, an alumnus of the Chanel x BIFF Asian Film Academy, saw his film “Elephants in the Fog” (2026) win the Jury Prize in Un Certain Regard at Cannes. Lee moved from theater acting and producing into filmmaking, directing “A Perm” (2009), “A Leave” (2020) and “The Final Semester” (2024), telling stories built around women who have crossed borders for work, employees pushed out of their jobs, and young people just starting their careers.
	

	The Netpac Award, presented by the Network for the Promotion of Asian Cinema to an outstanding film in the Vision section, will be judged by Nina Kochelyaeva, Matthew Poon and Lee Dongha. Kochelyaeva heads the Department for the Development and Approbation of Film Education Methods at VGIK, the Gerasimov Institute of Cinematography, and has served on selection committees at multiple festivals as a scholar, documentary filmmaker and programmer. Poon is senior project manager at HKIFF Industry and has appeared as a juror and speaker across international festivals and markets. Lee, CEO of Redpeter Films and chairperson of the Producers Guild of Korea, co-produced “Poetry” (2010) and “Hwayi: A Monster Boy” (2013) and produced “Train to Busan” (2016), “Another Child” (2019) and “Peninsula” (2020), along with “Dora” (2026), part of this year’s BIFF selection.

	The Fipresci Award, given by the Fédération Internationale de la Presse Cinématographique to a Vision section film for artistic achievement, will be judged by Ma Xingxu, Teresa Vena and Roh Chul-hwan. Ma is a film critic and editor whose work spans festival reporting and in-depth interviews focused on contemporary auteur cinema. Vena trained in history, art history and Spanish philology at university in Geneva before building a career split between Berlin and Switzerland, where she writes and curates across art and film and takes on jury and programming work at festivals internationally. Roh teaches theater and film studies at Inha University, where his scholarship centers on policy questions facing the film and media industries alongside the study of visual storytelling.

	The 31st Busan International Film Festival will run Oct. 6-15 at the Busan Cinema Center and venues throughout Busan, with the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market held Oct. 10-13.

schema.headline: Busan Names Jury Members for Mecenat, Sonje, Netpac, Fipresci Awards

title: Peter Jackson’s Weta FX to Talk AI as Netflix’s Creative Asia Spotlights ‘Possible Love’ in Busan
description: Netflix and the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) are bringing back Creative Asia for a third consecutive year, with the program set for Oct.
body:
Netflix and the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) are bringing back Creative Asia for a third consecutive year, with the program set for Oct. 10 at Dongseo University’s Centum Campus.

	BIFF, the Asian Film Commissions Network (AFCNet) and the Motion Picture Association (MPA) all helped shape this year’s lineup. 

	Creative Asia is Netflix’s flagship initiative for helping emerging Asian creators develop their ideas for the screen. This year marks the first time the program will include workshops, giving aspiring writers direct access to Netflix content executives.
	

	Netflix and the MPA co-host “AI in Filmmaking: New Tools, New Possibilities,” a panel on how AI is being adopted across the APAC filmmaking industry. Moderated by film critic Youn Sung-eun, the panel brings together Sung Q Lee, Netflix’s senior director of APAC production; Kimball Thurston, chief technology officer at Weta FX, the visual effects studio co-founded by Peter Jackson; and director Kang Yun-sung (“Run to the West,” “The Outlaws”).


	Cinematographer Kim Ji-yong will deliver a masterclass on shaping the visual world of Venice winner “Possible Love,” walking through the choices he made with director Lee Chang-dong, including trading artificial lighting setups for natural light, with scenes from the film used to illustrate his points. The film is playing at BIFF.

	The masterclass slate opens with “Location and Storytelling,” moderated by Busan Asian Film School professor James Bang, with input from Lauren Cooper of the Location Managers Guild International, “Perfect Days” producer Reiko Kunieda and Sung Q Lee. Director Han Jun-hee, known for “D.P. 1 & 2,” “Weak Hero Class 1 & 2” and “The Blue Road,” follows with a session on shaping unexpected material into resonant stories.
	

	Industry panels also include “New Voices in Filmmaking: What’s Ahead,” moderated by BIFF programmer Jeong Jihye, featuring Namkoong Sun (“Love Untangled,” “Time to Be Strong”) alongside “My Aunt” co-directors Wi Eun-kyoung and Son Gwang-min, whose short film won the Grand Prize at Korea’s 2026 Mise-en-scène Short Film Festival. An invite-only Creative Economy Exchange will also run.

	The two new workshops are led by Netflix content executives. Christopher Mack, the streamer’s director of content acquisition, leads “The Art and Archetypes of Cinematic Storytelling,” while Keo Lee, Netflix’s director of creative strategy, leads “Understanding the Buyer’s Perspective,” covering how projects get greenlit and financed.

	The event builds on two prior editions with BIFF and a stop last year in Indonesia at the JAFF Market, extending Netflix’s push to deepen ties with regional creative communities.

schema.headline: Peter Jackson’s Weta FX to Talk AI as Netflix’s Creative Asia Spotlights ‘Possible Love’ in Busan

title: Cate Blanchett to Attend Tokyo Festival for Japan Premiere of Displacement Film Fund Shorts
description: Cate Blanchett will travel to Tokyo for the 39th edition of the Tokyo International Film Festival, where five short films backed by the Displacement
body:
Cate Blanchett will travel to Tokyo for the 39th edition of the Tokyo International Film Festival, where five short films backed by the Displacement Film Fund will receive their Japan premieres. 

	Blanchett co-founded the Displacement Film Fund, which supports displaced filmmakers and those with a demonstrated history of telling authentic stories rooted in the experiences of displaced people. The fund was announced at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in January 2025 in partnership with IFFR’s Hubert Bals Fund, which serves as managing partner. UNHCR acts as strategic partner, with additional backing from Amahoro Coalition, Master Mind, the Tamer Family Foundation, Uniqlo – a founding partner – and Droom en Daad, a Dutch cultural foundation. The SP Lohia Foundation came aboard as a major partner when the second edition of the fund was confirmed at IFFR 2026.
	

	Blanchett said: “I am privileged to have the opportunity to share the inaugural short films supported through the Displacement Film Fund with audiences at Tokyo International Film Festival. In a world where conflict and persecution are driving displacement and division, cinematic storytelling has a vital role to play in connecting with the experiences of others. Being displaced shouldn’t mean filmmakers abandon their creativity; in fact their stories may feel even more urgent.”


	Following the screening, Blanchett will participate in a Q&A alongside two of the five directors whose work is included in the program: Mohammad Rasoulof, whose “Sense of Water” centers on an Iranian writer confronting a foreign language in exile, and Shahrbanoo Sadat, director of “Super Afghan Gym,” which is set in a downtown Kabul gym during the one hour each day reserved for women.
	

	The other three films in the selection are “Allies in Exile” (U.K./Syria), directed by Hasan Kattan, which follows two Syrian filmmakers documenting the trauma of waiting for asylum; “Rotation” (Ukraine/Turkey), directed by Maryna Er Gorbach, depicting a therapeutic hypnosis ritual experienced by a young Ukrainian woman who transitioned from civilian life to military service; and “Whispers of a Burning Scent” (Somalia/Austria/Germany), directed by Mo Harawe, in which a quiet wedding musician finds his private life drawn into public view.

	Blanchett’s Tokyo visit coincides with a separate honor: she is to receive the Praemium Imperiale Award during the same week. She recently wrapped production on Alice Birch’s “Sweetsick” and is in development with Janicza Bravo on a film about Martha Stewart. Her feature “Father Mother Sister Brother” (2025), which won the Golden Lion at the 82nd Venice Film Festival, is scheduled for Japanese theatrical release on Nov. 20.

	The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival is hosted by Unijapan and takes place Oct. 26 to Nov. 4.

schema.headline: Cate Blanchett to Attend Tokyo Festival for Japan Premiere of Displacement Film Fund Shorts

title: Does Stephen Colbert Miss Late Night TV?: ‘Nope!’
description:
Sep 15, 2026 9:38pm PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									AFP via Getty Images
	

		
	
				
	Hot off his Emmy win for outstanding variety se
body:
Sep 15, 2026 9:38pm PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									AFP via Getty Images
	

		
	
				
	Hot off his Emmy win for outstanding variety series, Stephen Colbert went on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” Tuesday night and revealed if he ever thinks about returning to late night television.

	“Late night TV. I remember it well. Many fond memories of this,” Colbert said while taking the stage. “Do you ever think about it?” Kimmel asked, to which Colbert responded: “Nope!”

	The Emmy-winner continued to remark about the fact that he no longer has to “think about the news every day,” to which Kimmel pointed out that Colbert seemed “like a different person,” “happier” and “healthier” when he saw the former host at the Emmys Monday night.
	

	“Like I don’t drink a cup of poison every day?” Colbert responded. “A good part of the job is, as I remember it, to be lowered like carbon rods into a radioactive pool every day. And then to be pulled out and put in front of a camera. And to radiate it back at the audience at a nonlethal rad level.”Speaking with CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh after the Emmy Awards, Colbert said free speech in is “alive and well” and thinks late-night is still a crucial part of the television ecosystem, despite the genre’s challenges in recent years.


	“Because if you can’t say something because you go to jail, that is a violation of free speech,” Colbert said. “I think that late night is just as funny and just as vital as it ever has been, and I love watching Jimmy and Jimmy and John and John and Seth and everybody else. And I think I hope it goes on for a long time because you get to work with people like this, and that’s the greatest gift.”

	“The Late Show With Stephen Colbert” ended in May after CBS announced the series’ cancellation.
	

	“The Late Show” took home its first outstanding variety series on Monday night for its final season. It competed in the category against “The Daily Show” (Comedy Central), “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” (ABC), “Last Week Tonight With John Oliver” (HBO Max) and “Saturday Night Live” (NBC).


	
		More from Variety

title: Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ for International Features Race
description: “La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s submission for the 2027 international feature film Academy
body:
“La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s submission for the 2027 international feature film Academy Award.

	Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved, ”starring Javier Bardem, and Alauda Ruiz de Azua’s Goya and San Sebastián winner “Sundays” also figured in Spain’s international feature shortlist, arguably the strongest in Spanish history.


	Any other Oscar entry choice from Spain than “La Bola Negra,” announced Wednesday by Alejandro Amenábar on behalf of Spain’s Academia de Cine, would have been a huge shock.
	

	Amenábar, whose “The Sea Inside” won Spain’s most recent international feature Oscar in 2005, opened the envelope and announced “La Bola Negra” at the Academia de Cine’s Madrid headquarters.


	The choice came after a second-round vote by Academy members, following the Sept. 3 selection of “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Sundays” as the country’s three shortlisted titles.

	World premiering in Cannes main competition, “La Bola Negra” first caught attention by scoring a 16 minute standing ovation at its world premiere on the Croisette. It caused a further splash winning best director, shared with Paweł Pawlikowski for “Fatherland.” 

	Picked up by Netflix for the U.S. and later Canada, “La Bola Negra” again moved waves when Netflix announced that it would open the feature theatrically on Oct. 16, setting a 47-day U.S. theatrical window the longest form any movie in the streaming giant’s history, a sure indication that the film will feature strongly among the streamer’s awards priorities for the fall.
	

	Though already regarded as one of the frontrunners in the international feature film category, “La Bola Negra” is already being talked up as a candidate for multiple other categories. “La Bola Negra’ has mucho heat,” Variety has asseverated. 

	Sweeping, unapologetically passionate and hugely ambitious, “La Bola Negra” braids three connected stories, each shot in a different film style, chronicling the travails and legacy of Spain’s gay experience in 1932, 1937 during the Spanish Civil War, and 2017. It picks up on the first four pages in an unfinished novel by legendary poet-playwright Federico García Lorca, bludgeoned and shot to death by Franco’s troops in 1936 for being a social activist and homosexual, “un maricón” in the Spanish macho slur.

	The film features a feisty turn from Penélope Cruz as a cabaret dancer and a cameo from Glenn Close as a modern-day hispanist, accompanying Spanish stars Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Milo Quifes and Carlos Gutiérrez in lead roles.

	From the get-go, the Javis set out to make “a super production that is auteur-driven but also very queer,” Ambrossi told Variety before the Cannes world premiere.

	Heavily researched, “La Bola Negra” reflects not only the ambitions of Los Javis, as its writer-director are known, but also Movistar Plus, the biggest Spanish pay TV/SVOD operator which produced with Los Javis newly launched Suma Content Films. It is co-produced by Pedro and Agustín Almodovar’s El Deseo and France’s Le Pacte, with the participation of Spanish network Atresmedia. Sales agent Goodfellas has practically sold out the world.

	After “lighting up” Telluride, Variety has reported, “La Bola Negra,” the film bowed Tuesday in Toronto. It won the Audience Award at Australia Sydney Festival, will open New York’s LGBTQ+ film festival NewFest on Oct. 15.  “La Bola Negra” will have is Spanish premiere at the San Sebastián Festival on Saturday, where it has already sparked a feeding fever for tickets.

	The shortlist for the 2027 Oscar nominations will be announced by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on Dec. 15, with the final selection announced on Jan. 21. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony is scheduled to take place on March 14 in Los Angeles.

schema.headline: Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ for International Features Race

title: Drake Unveils Surreal ‘Fear of Missing Out’ Film Featuring New Music Videos, Songs and an Ella Langley Remix
description: Drake debuted “Fear of Missing Out” on Tuesday night, unveiling an hourlong string of music videos, new songs and scenes featuring a spate of guests
body:
Drake debuted “Fear of Missing Out” on Tuesday night, unveiling an hourlong string of music videos, new songs and scenes featuring a spate of guests including Sexyy Red, Winnie Harlow, Lena the Plug, Don Toliver and his mother, Sandi Graham.

	The livestream, which Drake had previously described as a “not so short film,” indeed lived up to his promise as he rolled out clips set to songs from his recent albums “Maid of Honour” and “Habibti.” “FOMO” was directed by Theo Skudra, Liam Macrae, Jake Schreier, Zong Li and Glenn Michael, and was presented as a surrealist assortment of visuals that Drake had clearly captured throughout the year in his native Toronto and beyond.
	



	It began with “Cheetah Print” alongside Sexyy Red before Drake hit the beach with Stunna Sandy for “Outside Tweaking,” giving way to an infomercial tutorial on how to make the drink “Panty Dropper.” During the film, Harlow starred in the video for “New Bestie” while Drake’s mom Sandi showed off her new “Icemom” tattoo in the clip for “True Bestie.”


	Among the videos for previously released songs were “WNBA,” “Road Trips” and “Hoe Phase,” all songs included on his recent records. But he snuck in a few new tracks, namely his highly suspected remix of Ella Langley’s history-making hit “Choosin’ Texas.” Drake’s take on the tune was a slowed-down, underwater rendition that corralled Don Toliver and featured the chorus, “Drinkin’ yak all by myself / She’s from Texas I can tell.”

	Drake also unveiled another new song with Toliver as well as one with Yeat. The film came to a conclusion with a full-circle moment as Drake stood in a set piece ripped straight from the video for “Hotline Bling,” and ended with a stagehand bringing out a stepladder for Drake to exit the set. After “FOMO” debuted, the YouTube stream was set to private.
	

	Fans have long speculated if “Fear of Missing Out” would be an album, music video or even a tour. But this past weekend, Drake dropped a teaser on Instagram and described it as a “not so short film directed and scored by the family.”

	On Monday, he elaborated on what exactly the project would be, explaining that it’s “self funded surrealism” and “a story about making the absolute most of it all in one summer.”

	“Here’s some life advice before you watch,” he wrote in an Instagram post. “Nobody is coming to save you. You must use each day to decipher who you love and trust and march forward with themI hope this serves as motivation to make that call, take that trip, drop that song, open that shop, see your parents, leave that relationship or stay in it forever, spend the bread, get some more etc.

	“They keep saying our genre is dying,” he continued. “Videos don’t matter. Nobody is watching nobody is listening. I still care. As much as I did on the set of Best I Ever Had. So be kind and rewind.”

	Drake dropped “Fear of Missing Out” on the back of an already stacked year, which included a trio of albums — “Iceman,” “Maid of Honour” and “Habibti” — that dropped as a surprise in May. The projects had a total of 43 songs and guest appearances from a slew of artists including Future, 21 Savage, Sexyy Red, Central Cee, PartyNextDoor and more.

	He had been teasing “Iceman” as early as 2024, and started concretely previewing it in July 2025 with the livestream “Iceman Episode 1” on YouTube. He announced the three albums just after the conclusion of a fourth installment of the “Iceman” livestream series in May.

schema.headline: Drake Unveils Surreal ‘Fear of Missing Out’ Film Featuring New Music Videos, Songs and an Ella Langley Remix

title: ‘Vivant’ Tops Asia Streaming Chart, First Japanese Drama to Lead, Report Finds
description: TBS drama “Vivant” outdrew every other streaming title across Asia last month, excluding China and India, becoming the first Japanese show to top am
body:
TBS drama “Vivant” outdrew every other streaming title across Asia last month, excluding China and India, becoming the first Japanese show to top ampd Analytics’ regional monthly ranking since the measurement firm began tracking the market. 

	The finding comes from a new ampd Vision report titled “Vivant: A TV Broadcast Hit, Streamed.”

	“Vivant,” which launched its second season in July as part of TBS’s Sunday Theater slot, pulled in 15.6 million unique viewers regionwide in August, with 15.1 million watching in Japan alone. That figure equals a quarter of the 61.4 million viewers ampd tracks across Japanese VOD, according to the report from ampd Analytics, the streaming measurement arm of Media Partners Asia (MPA).
	

	The series follows Yusuke Nogi, a Japanese trading company employee drawn into an international conspiracy tied to a shadowy government intelligence unit known as Beppan. Season 2 picks up immediately after the first season’s cliffhanger and was shot partly on location in Azerbaijan.


	Much of that reach came through TVer, the free platform operated by Japan’s broadcast networks, which drew 10.2 million of the show’s viewers. Only two other titles have ever pulled 10 million viewers on one platform in a single market within a month, according to ampd: broadcasts of the World Baseball Classic in Japan and the Korean drama “Teach You a Lesson,” both distributed on Netflix. TBS made the new season available on TVer at no cost within an hour of its Sunday broadcast, reserving paid streaming exclusively for U-Next. That arrangement created a second viewing peak each week, on Monday nights, and 92% of viewers who came back for a new episode had already watched the previous one by the time it aired.
	

	The show’s popularity also lifted viewership of its first season elsewhere. Netflix’s audience for “Vivant” grew more than eightfold between May and August, from 300,000 viewers to 2.5 million, while U-Next’s viewership rose over the same period from 100,000 to 2 million. That shift happened even among subscribers who already had access to the show elsewhere: an estimated one in eight Prime Video subscribers and one in 10 Netflix subscribers in Japan chose to watch “Vivant” on TVer rather than on the services they already pay for.

	Beyond the streaming platforms, “Vivant” built a substantial following on YouTube, where related content drew 13.2 million viewers, nearly matching its VOD reach. That audience was spread across more than 1,600 videos posted by 450 channels, totaling 8.8 million hours watched at an average of almost 40 minutes per viewer. A companion show TBS produced alongside the drama, “Villains’ Meeting Room,” averaged more than 1.3 million viewers an episode.

	“‘Vivant’ is a distribution story as much as a content story,” said Sam Yousif, managing director of ampd Analytics. “A quarter of Japan’s tracked VOD audience watched one drama in a single month, and premium subscribers moved to a free platform to follow it. Japan is the largest VOD market we measure, with the closest relationship between broadcast and streaming anywhere in the region, and measuring a title today means measuring it everywhere it lives, including YouTube, where ‘Vivant’ reached almost as many people as it did on VOD.”

	The drama’s success did not extend much beyond Japan’s borders. Some 97% of all “Vivant” viewing came from local audiences, ampd found, a pattern consistent with Japanese dramas’ broader struggles abroad: they land in Netflix’s global top 10 outside Japan just 0.3 times a month on average, well behind Korean dramas at 4.1 times and Japanese anime at 1.4.

schema.headline: ‘Vivant’ Tops Asia Streaming Chart, First Japanese Drama to Lead, Report Finds

body:
Melissa McCarthy
                          Morphs Into JonBenét Ramsey's Mom
                          For New Flick
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen were seen for the first time as JonBenét Ramsey's parents in a photo from the upcoming TV film about the slain beauty queen.
      
    
            The actors are set to star as JonBenét's parents, Patsy and John, in Netflix’s "The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey." The photo shows the actors recreating a famous interview with the couple given months after JonBenét died.
      
    
            JonBenét was found dead inside her family home on December 26, 1996. The police never found who murdered the 6-year-old.
      
    
            Her parents fought off intense backlash over the situation for years ... with some blaming them for their daughter's death, which they adamantly denied.

            The "Mamma Mia" star and Thomas wed in 2017. Amanda praised Thomas in an interview with Vogue earlier this year.
